slides.title: Where expertise becomes opportunity
slides.lead: Helping polygraph professionals grow, build reputation, expand their network, and unlock new opportunities.
slides.footer: A global ecosystem for polygraph professionals
slides.note: We succeed when our professionals get tangible value. This is a stakeholder vision, not a validated fundraising pitch. Detelgy enables opportunities; it does not guarantee clients, income, professional standing or improved examination accuracy. Original promise: Helping polygraph professionals grow their expertise, reputation, connections and income opportunities.

slides.title:
A global profession.
Still disconnected.
slides.lead: Profiles, clients, peers, and learning still live in separate places.
slides.footer: Working hypothesis · sources in speaker notes
slides.note: The APA provides a professional directory and educational seminars, demonstrating existing channels. The broader fragmentation framing is a hypothesis from the supplied briefs, not a measured industry-wide finding. No market size is asserted. Four visual fragments group the existing channels: visibility (websites, directories and social), clients (referrals), peers (messaging groups and associations), and learning (seminars). Existing networks already provide value. Working hypothesis · sources in speaker notes. Validate the fragmentation framing through expert discovery and market learning.
sources: American Polygraph Association: prospective member resources and seminars. Accessed 15 October 2026. https://www.polygraph.org/for_prospective_members.php
slides.prompt: What if expertise could move between them?

One ambition to grow.

slides.note: These are behavioral archetypes, not demographic segments. Commercially active independent examiners are the initial ICP hypothesis. Institutional examiners may have restrictions on commercial work. Prioritize useful local density over claims of global marketplace liquidity. Strategic audience hypotheses · initial country focus: Ukraine and Spain. These are complementary audiences, not Basic / Specialist / Master levels or a fixed progression. The independent examiner is the primary ICP; emerging professionals and established experts create value alongside them. sources: ICP / Personas §§2–7; Product brief §§4, 9; Investor story S03.

slides.title:
Experienced. Respected.
Ready for the next chapter.
slides.footer: Fictional composite persona · motivations are hypotheses, not interview findings
slides.note: The portrait is AI-generated and does not depict an actual Detelgy member. The persona is a composite based on the supplied brief, with an illustrative name, age, location and experience added for storytelling at the founder’s request. These details are fictional, not member data or interview findings. No income or performance result is asserted. The potential first value is a useful professional connection or a qualified inquiry. Fictional composite persona · motivations are hypotheses, not interview findings. David, 41, represents an experienced independent polygraph examiner in Kyiv, Ukraine, with 12 years in practice and a successful local practice. This is fictional narrative context, not a verified Detelgy customer or performance claim. This slide introduces his identity and aspirations; Slide 05 covers the barriers.

slides.title:
More than a polygraph expert.
He's running his own business.
slides.lead: From examinations and clients to administration and continuous learning, David has to manage it all.

items.title: Professional Practice
items.body: Conduct examinations, manage cases and deliver quality services.

items.title: Marketing & Clients
items.body: Build visibility, attract clients and maintain a trusted reputation.

items.title: Business Management
items.body: Handle bookings, payments, workflows and daily administration.

items.title: Professional Growth
items.body: Learn from peers, exchange knowledge and develop new skills.

slides.footer: Illustrative workflow hypothesis · experiences vary by professional and market
slides.note: The four cards represent different responsibilities, not nonexistent support. Associations and established communities already create value. Expert Discovery interviews should test which connections are missing or costly for each segment. Illustrative workflow hypothesis · experiences vary by professional and market. David is a fictional illustrative persona, not a verified customer. His workload represents competing responsibilities and limited time, not a lack of professional skill or total absence of support. The four responsibilities cover professional practice, marketing and clients, business management, and professional growth. The AI-generated illustration adapts the Slide 04 portrait; it is not a customer photograph. This slide describes the responsibilities of an independent examiner, not Detelgy’s currently available features. Future solution slides must distinguish verified current capabilities from roadmap proposals, especially CRM, internal payments, automation, mentorship and training. A responsibility shown here does not imply that Detelgy currently provides that capability.

slides.title:
You already have the expertise.
But growth isn't automatic.
slides.lead: Three barriers can stand between your expertise and your next opportunity.
slides.footer: Illustrative research hypotheses · these are not customer quotations
slides.note: These pains are hypotheses from the supplied audience brief. Validate urgency, frequency, existing alternatives and willingness to pay through Expert Discovery. Do not present the first-person questions as verbatim testimony. Illustrative research hypotheses · these are not customer quotations. These three barriers are illustrative hypotheses, not universal conditions: established networks may already provide useful visibility, peers and opportunities. The earlier six exploratory pains grouped here were: Professional isolation, Limited discoverability, Scattered trust signals, Learning barriers, Uncertain client flow, Narrow earning paths. They require segment-specific validation through expert discovery. None is a claim that David or every examiner lacks professional skill.

slides.title: What does professional success look like?
slides.footer: Working JTBD hypotheses · paid peer services and education are planned
slides.note: These four Jobs To Be Done are illustrative professional aspirations, not verified outcomes for every Detelgy user. One person can have several ambitions, and priorities can change over time; this is not a mandatory sequence. Detelgy may enable access to opportunities, but does not guarantee income growth, client demand, or professional recognition. Paid consultation, mentorship and education mechanisms are planned and require demand validation. Working JTBD hypotheses · paid peer services and education are planned.

slides.title:
Same expertise.
A world of new possibilities.
slides.lead: Detelgy connects the people, tools and opportunities that support professional growth.
slides.footer: Intended transformation · access to opportunity does not guarantee outcomes
slides.note: This is an intended, illustrative transformation, not a verified result for every examiner. The same fictional David appears in both states; the contrast does not imply he lacks skill before joining Detelgy. The comparative line lengths are illustrative visual emphasis, not measured performance or quantified outcomes. Profiles, discussions, community networking, service discovery and request flows are reported as a built foundation in the internal brief, but production readiness and professional outcomes still require validation. Publications, paid transactions, consultations, mentorship and education are planned; do not describe them as live. Access to opportunity does not guarantee clients, income growth or professional standing. The earlier five comparisons were: local circle to broader discovery; isolated knowledge to peer learning; scattered credentials to one profile; recognition within existing circles to visible contributions; and personal-service income to potential consulting, mentorship or teaching.

slides.title: From joining to growing.
slides.lead: The first valuable moment is different for every professional.
slides.footer: Illustrative, non-linear journey · first-value moments are hypotheses
slides.note: Participation can create professional value without a paid transaction. Journeys may start at different points, loop or branch. A profile view is not a qualified lead, and activity is not proof of career improvement. Full underlying journey: Discover → Join → Participate → Connect & learn → Build reputation → Find opportunities → Earn / lead → Refer & contribute. The five visual milestones group this eight-step model; the route is illustrative, not a growth metric. Illustrative, non-linear journey · first-value moments are hypotheses.
slides.diagramAlt: A rising curved route links Discover, Join, Connect, Build reputation and Grow. Connect is the focal stage.

slides.title:
Every meaningful contribution
can create more value
slides.lead: Useful knowledge can build visibility and trust. Relevant opportunities can give people a reason to return.
slides.footer: Proposed mechanism · not a demonstrated network effect
slides.note: Every arrow is a hypothesis to measure. There is no guarantee that contributing increases orders. Test contribution-to-profile discovery, relevant relationships, attributed inquiries and repeat meaningful participation. Proposed mechanism · not a demonstrated network effect.

slides.title:
Professional success
has more than one path
slides.lead: A stronger practice. A wider impact. A lasting contribution.
slides.footer: Complementary paths, not ranks · some mechanisms are planned
slides.note: Industry Leader recognition is distinct from transaction-based levels and does not automatically confer Master status. Professionals can follow more than one path. Teaching and paid peer consulting belong to phased expansion. Complementary paths, not ranks · some mechanisms are planned.
sources: Product brief §§7, 11; ICP / Personas §12; Investor story S12.
